Bug_Title: SING: Class using singleton design pattern indirectly implements Cloneable interface. (SING_SINGLETON_INDIRECTLY_IMPLEMENTS_CLONEABLE)
Bug_Details:
If a class using singleton design pattern indirectly implements the Cloneable interface, it is possible to create a copy of the object, thus violating the singleton pattern.
Therefore, implementing the Cloneable interface should be avoided. If that's not possible because of an extended super-class, the solution would be overriding the clone method to unconditionally throw CloneNotSupportedException.

For more information, see: SEI CERT MSC07-J.
Bug_Explanation: The SingletonCloneable class inherits from SuperCloneable which implements the Cloneable interface. This makes SingletonCloneable indirectly implement Cloneable, allowing the singleton instance to be cloned, which violates the singleton pattern.
Trigger_Explanation: The test case calls the showBug() method of the SingletonCloneableDemo class, which attempts to clone a singleton instance. Since the SingletonCloneable class indirectly implements the Cloneable interface, the clone method can be invoked, violating the singleton pattern and triggering the bug.
